newsitem.title: USA: Planar sees Q4 results below forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Planar sees Q4 results below forecasts.

text.p: Planar Systems Inc said it expects financial results for the fourth quarter ending September 27 to fall significantly below analyst's expectations.

It cited lower-than-expected revenues in its government sales, combined with additional engineering expenses for both new product development and manufacturing improvements, as the basis for its likely shortfall in earnings for the fourth quarter.
First Call's mean consensus of fourth quarter estimates is $0.23 a share versus $0.25 a share a year ago.
Planar is the sole-source supplier of CRT cockpit displays for the U.S. government's F-18 and B-2 bombers.

Delays in order receipts in the fourth quarter are expected to move projected revenues into its next fiscal year, it said. Planar plans to report its fourth quarter results November 6. Third quarter earnings were $2.1 million, or 19-cents per share, on sales of $19.5 million.
"What has been more difficult is the decision to sustain a very aggressive investment in new product development despite its near-term added pressure on our earnings.

"The combination of our continued development of a new generation of displays together with the continued reduction of manufacturing costs is our number-one priority to return us to sustained growth," said Jim Hurd, chief executive officer.
